D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: debug print statement left in the lexer
where should output/error printing happen
can the interpreter module print directly
req-0317.statement: No `print()`/`sys.stdout.write`/`sys.stderr.write` outside `bract/cli.py` — the lexer, parser, and evaluator modules communicate exclusively through return values and raised exceptions.

hints: adding a new top-level script for a CLI subcommand
where does argument parsing for bract fmt live
req-06f1.statement: All three CLI entry points (`bract`, `bract run FILE`, `bract fmt FILE`) are dispatched from a single `bract/__main__.py` — there is no second top-level script or console-script entry point.

hints: comparing two strings with <
can booleans be compared with less-than
implicit numeric coercion in arithmetic
req-09dd.statement: Ordering comparisons (< > <= >=) and arithmetic (+ - * /) operate only on two Integers — applying them to strings, booleans, or nil is always a runtime type error, never a lexicographic or truthiness comparison.

hints: does Bract support /* */ comments
block comment syntax
multi-line comments
req-153d.statement: `//` starts a line comment that runs to end of line; there are no block comments in Bract.

hints: using + to concatenate strings
string concatenation operator
why does "a" + "b" throw a type error
req-1a96.statement: `~` concatenates two strings only (`line N: '~' expects strings` otherwise). `+` is exclusively integer addition — applying it to any string operand is a type error `line N: '+' cannot be applied to strings`, never concatenation.

hints: how do I run the tests for this project
test runner command
req-1e0b.statement: Run the test suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

hints: should the REPL exit after a runtime error
handling an error in interactive mode
req-24cc.statement: The REPL does not exit on a per-statement error — it reports the error the same way as any other error path and continues reading the next statement.

hints: can I use this pip package here
is a third-party library ok for this
should I add this to requirements.txt
need a package for JSON parsing or regex helpers
req-26a9.statement: Bract targets Python standard library only — never import, pip install, or list a third-party package as a dependency, anywhere in the implementation.

hints: the task prompt contradicts DESIGN.md, which do I follow
spec and ticket disagree
req-2e78.statement: Where DESIGN.md and a task description conflict, treat the conflict as a bug to flag, not license to guess.

hints: why is at(s, 0) out of range
off-by-one in string indexing
porting a 0-indexed algorithm to Bract's builtins
req-3f80.statement: String builtins (`len`, `at`, `sub`) are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed. `at("hello", 1)` is "h"; `at("hello", 0)` is out of range — there is no character at index 0.

hints: let inside a while loop body erroring as already declared
per-iteration scope in a loop
does a block scope persist across loop iterations
req-4813.statement: A new lexical scope is created fresh every time a block is entered — each `while` iteration and each function call starts with an empty innermost scope, so a `let` inside a loop body declares anew each iteration rather than colliding with the previous iteration's binding.

hints: does bract fmt rewrite the file in place
can the formatter change operator precedence or expression grouping
formatter reordering statements
req-4ab8.statement: `bract fmt FILE` only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement — it never reorders, re-associates, or drops AST nodes — and it never modifies the source file itself, only writes the formatted result to stdout.

hints: where do I write up the audit findings
should I create a new markdown file for this report
documenting standing constraint fixes
req-4b06.statement: Standing-constraint audit results (which SC items required a fix) are reported in the PR/commit description, not written up as a new doc.

hints: off-by-one in the reported error line number
is the line counter 0- or 1-indexed
req-57b3.statement: Source line numbers surfaced in any error message are always 1-indexed, matching how every text editor numbers lines.

hints: should a < b < c parse like Python's chained comparison
supporting chained comparisons
range check syntax a < x < b
req-5be8.statement: The `comparison` grammar rule accepts at most one comp-op — chained comparisons like `a < b < c` must fail to parse with `line N: comparisons do not chain`, not silently associate like Python. The workaround is explicit parenthesization: `(a < b) and (b < c)`.

hints: should bract run print the value of the last expression
REPL vs script output behavior
req-5dfa.statement: `bract run FILE` produces no output beyond what the program itself produces — there is no implicit "result" printing the way the REPL does.

hints: what naming convention for token types
should TokenType members be PascalCase or snake_case
req-6495.statement: Token type names in the lexer are SCREAMING_CASE (LET, IDENT, INT, STRING, PLUS, TILDE, NOTEQ, ...).

hints: could I just eval() this expression
shortcut the evaluator with exec
compile the AST to a python code object
req-656f.statement: No use of Python eval, exec, or compile anywhere in bract/ — the interpreter must be a genuine tree-walker over its own AST, not a translation layer onto Python's.

hints: writing the README for a language feature
should I document the full grammar in user docs
keeping README and DESIGN.md in sync
where do I explain operator precedence to users
avoiding spec duplication in documentation
req-67b7.statement: User-facing docs like README.md must not restate the full grammar or semantics; they should point to DESIGN.md instead.

hints: should sub raise when start is greater than end
empty substring range handling
req-799c.statement: `sub` with `start > end` returns `""` rather than raising an error, as long as both bounds are individually valid — the range is just empty.

hints: should mismatched types be coerced instead of erroring
implicit int-to-string conversion in an operator
req-7fa6.statement: There is no implicit type conversion anywhere in Bract — a type mismatch on any operator or builtin is always a runtime type error, never silent coercion.

hints: does and/or short-circuit in Bract
guarding a call with x != nil and f(x)
side effects in the right operand of or
req-8074.statement: `and`/`or` always evaluate both operands, left-to-right, regardless of the left operand's value — there is no short-circuit evaluation. A non-boolean operand is a runtime error `line N: operand of 'and'/'or' must be a boolean`.

hints: does bract run execute partially before a parse error
why would a syntax error later in the file still block all output
bract run exit code 2 vs exit code 1
partial execution before parse error
req-8191.statement: `bract run FILE` must fully lex and parse the entire file before executing any of it: a lex or parse error anywhere in the file exits with code 2 and the program must not have begun executing.

hints: do I need a test for the chained-comparison error
what edge cases should the parser tests cover
is happy-path coverage enough for a new grammar rule
req-86f2.statement: New language-feature tests must specifically cover the prior-trap edge cases (chained comparisons, non-short-circuit and/or, boolean-only conditions, 1-indexed builtins, etc.), not just the grammar's happy path.

hints: how should negative number division round
implementing modulo for negative operands
what happens on division by zero
req-8d02.statement: `%` is remainder defined so that `(a / b) * b + (a % b) == a`. The spec does not pin which direction `/` and `%` round for operands of differing sign, but an implementation must be internally consistent between the two operators. Division or remainder by zero is a runtime error `line N: division by zero`.

hints: can if(0) or if("") work like Python truthiness
treating nil as falsy in a condition
implicit boolean coercion for if/while
req-8eb0.statement: `if`/`while` conditions must evaluate to Boolean; any other type (0, "", nil) is a runtime type error `line N: condition must be a boolean` — there is no truthy/falsy coercion anywhere in Bract.

hints: is bract fmt supposed to be idempotent
running fmt twice changes the file
fmt of fmt output differs
formatter stability requirement
req-95ad.statement: `bract fmt` output must be byte-stable: formatting already-formatted source (fmt∘fmt) must be a no-op.

hints: where should this new module live
should I create a bract/core subpackage
organizing interpreter modules
splitting a big module into a subpackage
req-9af0.statement: Every interpreter module lives directly under bract/ (e.g. bract/lexer.py) — no nested subpackages like bract/lexer/ or bract/core/parser/.

hints: is it ok to leave a stub for later
raise NotImplementedError and call the task done
partial implementation with a TODO
req-9cf5.statement: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub left in any module reachable from bract/__main__.py once a task claims to have completed the feature that module implements.

hints: what should the repl prompt text be
ctrl-d crashes the repl
EOF handling in the bract repl
repl exit code when stdin closes
uncaught exception on Ctrl-D in REPL
req-a234.statement: The REPL prompt string is exactly "bract> " (with one trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) must end the REPL session cleanly with exit code 0 rather than raising an uncaught exception.

hints: where should a new error type live
adding an error class for the formatter
why is there a bract/errors.py
duplicate line N message formatting
which module owns error formatting
req-ab3e.statement: All Bract error types (LexError, ParseError, EvalError, and any future error type such as a formatter error) subclass a single BractError base defined in bract/errors.py, rather than each module defining its own line/message formatting inline.

hints: converting an integer to a string
is there a str() or int() builtin
mutating a string in place
req-b079.statement: There is no built-in for numeric<->string conversion, and no arithmetic on strings or string mutation anywhere in the language — `at`/`len`/`sub` are the entire string-manipulation surface.

hints: can I use a module-level global for the environment
where should call-stack state live
singleton interpreter state
req-b44e.statement: No module-level mutable interpreter state — no global dict/list holding variable bindings, call stack, or program output across calls. All interpreter state is threaded explicitly through function arguments/return values or held on an explicit Interpreter/Environment instance.

hints: implementing closures for fn values
does a returned function retain access to outer variables
counter/accumulator closure pattern
req-be1d.statement: `fn` values are real closures that close over their defining environment — a returned inner `fn` still sees its outer `let` bindings after the outer call returns.

hints: should I update DESIGN.md to reflect this fix
the spec seems wrong, can I edit it
where do spec corrections go
req-c15b.statement: DESIGN.md is frozen at seed-v1 and is never edited again after the freeze tag — later corrections to the implementation arrive only as task-prompt text, never as edits to DESIGN.md.

hints: can an existing variable be reassigned with just x = value
bare assignment statement
why does set exist separately from let
req-c1f5.statement: There is no bare `x = expr;` assignment form — an identifier followed directly by `=` outside a `let`/`set` keyword is a parse error.

hints: implementing not-equals as !=
should the parser handle != specially
why does != fail to lex
req-cedf.statement: There is no `!` or `!=` token/operator anywhere in Bract's grammar. A stray `!` is a lex error (`line N: unexpected character '!'`), and `!=` must never be special-cased at the parser — not-equals is spelled `<>` at the same precedence as `==`.

hints: RecursionError on deep bract recursion
how many levels of user recursion should bract support
can eval_expression call itself for nested calls
python recursion limit hit running a bract program
does the tree-walker need its own call stack
req-cf83.statement: The evaluator must be iterative with respect to Bract-level nesting/call depth: no Bract function call, nested block, or expression evaluation may consume Python call-stack frames proportional to user-controlled Bract call/nesting depth. Use explicit work-stacks instead of naive Python recursion so that arbitrarily deep Bract-level recursion or nesting cannot hit Python's own recursion limit.

hints: should I add s[0] indexing to the parser
bracket syntax for string access
array/string subscript operator
req-d1b1.statement: There is no subscript/index syntax (`s[0]`) anywhere in the grammar — string indexing exists only via the `at`/`sub` builtins. Don't add bracket parsing as a convenience.

hints: negative number division truncation vs floor
should % or / use python's // operator
division rounding for mixed sign operands
modulo of negative integers in bract
-7 / 2 what should it evaluate to
req-d1cf.statement: % is remainder defined so that (a / b) * b + (a % b) == a. Integer division (`/`) and remainder (`%`) truncate toward zero for operands of mixed sign -- do not implement them with Python's `/` or `//` directly, since neither truncates toward zero for negative operands. Division or remainder by zero is a runtime error `line N: division by zero`.

hints: an uncaught exception is printing a python traceback
multi-line error output
should error messages have colored output
req-d6d4.statement: Every lex/parse/runtime error is rendered as a single line on stderr, `line N: <message>`, sourced from one shared error-formatting path — never a Python traceback, exception class name, ANSI color, or secondary line.

hints: implementing sub like a python slice
off-by-one in substring end index
sub(s, 1, 3) returning the wrong length
req-d6f0.statement: `sub(s, start, end)` is inclusive on both ends and 1-indexed — `sub("hello", 1, 3)` is "hel". Do not copy Python's exclusive-end slice semantics (`"hello"[0:3]`).

hints: what escape sequences does a string literal support
adding \r or \0 escape
error message for a bad backslash escape
string runs off the end of the line
req-e10e.statement: String escapes recognize only ", \\, \n, and \t. Any other character after a backslash is a lex error `line N: unknown escape sequence '\x'`. An unterminated string (newline or EOF before the closing quote) is `line N: unterminated string`.

hints: what exit code should a type error produce
non-zero exit code for a lex error vs runtime error
req-f9a1.statement: Exit codes are exactly 0 (success), 1 (runtime error), or 2 (lex/parse error) — produced only by `bract run` and the top-level CLI dispatch. No other exit code is ever returned.

hints: redeclaring the same variable name with let twice
assigning to a variable that was never declared
shadowing vs redeclaration error
req-fca9.statement: `let x = expr;` declares a new binding in the current scope and errors `line N: 'x' is already declared` if x already exists in that exact scope (shadowing an outer scope's x with a new `let` is fine). `set x = expr;` reassigns an existing binding found by walking the scope chain outward, erroring `line N: 'x' is not declared` if none exists.
